rules.text: Explicit types — never `var`. Spell the type on every local (`List<string> ids = ...`). The only exception is a genuinely unnameable anonymous-type projection from EF/LINQ Select/GroupBy/ToDictionary. `.editorconfig` flags `var` as an error (IDE0008).

rules.text: Dashboard TypeScript: no annotation when the value already has the type (`const queries = useQueryClient()`, `computed(...)` without ComputedRef). Widen or narrow only through the generic (`ref<T | null>(null)`). A constant table is `{ ... } as const satisfies Record<K, V>`; a table read by a computed string key, an exported string-keyed table, or a list keeps its widening annotation. The lint rule app/no-redundant-type-annotation enforces it, and unused-imports/no-unused-imports deletes unused imports: run `eslint --fix`, never sweep by hand. Never write "explicit types on locals" in a dashboard brief.
rules.source: Stoney 2026-10-13: "don't type variables if the return type of the value matches and does not change for things like this: const queries: QueryClient = useQueryClient()"; "use a linter, don't do them by hand"; "use as const satisfies type"; "also add a linter that removes unused imports"; memory feedback-ts-no-redundant-annotations.md

rules.text: Dashboard layout: a ternary puts `? a` and `: b` on their own lines; an arrow whose body is a ternary starts it on the next line without brackets (app/arrow-ternary-body); an expression arrow that is the LAST call argument and shares its line with an earlier argument ends that line at `=>` and starts its body on the next line, one level in (app/trailing-arrow-argument; a lone or first callback, an arrow with more arguments after it, and a block body stay). An if body is a bare `return`/`break`/`continue` on the if line, a returned or thrown value on the next line one level in (no braces), or a braced block for anything else; a loop body (for, for-in, for-of, while, do) is always a braced block. A blank line sets apart each statement group, and every if, loop, switch and try. ESLint enforces it (@stylistic/multiline-ternary, operator-linebreak, indent, padding-line-between-statements, app/body-shape); Prettier undoes the ternary and if breaks, so format with `npm run format` (Prettier, then `eslint --fix`), never Prettier alone and never by hand.

session_only.text: Run up to 6 read-only agents and 2 that build or test at once (global rule). Keep both build lanes busy and the next slice briefed; never open 11 at once.

Every external API limiter takes its ceiling from one conservative provider-budget constant, and pollers take their cadence from that budget, never from a fixed interval. A guard test ties cadence x calls per tick <= ceiling <= provider budget.

A cross-channel mass ban reaches only channels that opted in: the owner's flag (Channel.AcceptsModeratorMassBans, off by default), the operator's own channel, a channel named as attacked, or a ModeratorMassBanOptIn row where the moderator recorded the streamer's word. Every other moderated channel is not_opted_in and gets no batch. Never widen reach without a recorded opt-in (Stoney 2026-10-06).

A cross-channel moderation action (mass ban) runs at once on the operator's own channel, every attacked channel and every offline channel; only a LIVE channel holds for !allow/!disallow (floor 20) or until the stream ends. Holding is the exception that needs a named reason, never the default. A notice the bot posts in another streamer's channel is formal: one text for every tone, no personality variants.

Every brief names its handoff path in the session scratchpad (C:/Users/patri/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Projects-NoMercyLabs-nomnomzbot/<session>/scratchpad/handoff-<slice>.md), never the main-tree .scratch (refused) or the worktree .scratch (deleted with an unchanged worktree). Builder briefs say: first code edit by tool call 6.
Push validated work in regular, properly sized batches: not every commit, not never. A batch boundary is when the in-flight feature lands. CI is watched in the background.
Worktrees, scratch checkouts and temp files stay inside the project root (worktrees under .claude/worktrees/, scratch under .scratch/), never as sibling directories. No exception for a live agent.
Backend user-facing strings carry a resource KEY only. The en and nl values live in strings.xml (values/ and values-nl/), never inline in C#.

Never send keystrokes or mouse input (SendKeys, AutoHotkey, UI Automation, xdotool) to the owner's machine. Live UI checks use test hooks, Compose UI tests, Playwright or a window the agent opened itself.
Never run git stash, checkout --, clean or reset on a shared tree with live agents. It sweeps everyone's uncommitted work. Recovery: git checkout stash@{0} -- <file>; never drop the stash.
A commit must compile on its own. Never commit code that reads a contract change you left unstaged: commit the contract with its consumer, or commit neither.
Never forward host secrets or credentials into a container, sandbox or dev environment. The user logs in inside the box. If a host secret is truly needed, ask first and explain the exposure.
Object-typed JSON columns: a Newtonsoft JToken passed through System.Text.Json mangles arrays to [] and objects to {}. Serialize with one library end to end.
Judge native commands by $LASTEXITCODE. Never 2>&1 under ErrorActionPreference=Stop: git/gh stderr progress becomes a terminating error.
Run dotnet csharpier format then check (pinned tool) before every commit, including in agent briefs.
Worktree agents can leak commits to the main tree. Verify each agent committed to ITS branch.
Never sweep worktrees. Remove one only after its agent completed and its work is integrated.
Doc reviews report substantive contradictions only, never nitpicks.
Never mutate live DB credentials. Diagnose read-only; ask before changing.
Never ask for a go before a test run, live tests on the box included. Check the facts yourself, have the rollback ready, run, report.
Blocked is not stop: never checkpoint at a block; work the other queued tasks.
Classify each new owner message: a correction means stop and fix now; an addition means finish the current task first.
Comments only explain complexity. Never write 'issues found' or history essays in code comments.
Work in small validated vertical slices; commit each one; never pile up uncommitted changes.
Use the watch-ci skill / scripts/push-and-watch.ps1 for every push, never hand-roll gh run watch
